brief: Morgan Stanley's equities desk (Nick Savone), via The Market Ear. The S&P 500 fell despite more than 80% of its stocks rising, the first such divergence in nearly 40 years, as single-stock volatility versus the index hit extraordinary levels and cross-stock correlation collapsed. Hedge funds have de-grossed 8% since June, the largest sustained reduction on record, and net leverage is back to 51% mainly on short covering, not conviction buying. Equal-weight stocks are outperforming as the Magnificent Seven stumble, raising the question of whether portfolio managers keep defending past winners into year-end or rotate broader. Europe's STOXX 600 is only about 3% below its highs, but cyclicals have underperformed defensives by 13% and momentum has unwound 14% since June, a rotational bear market Morgan Stanley says sets up a reversal in Semiconductors, Hardware and Banks. Mike Wilson sees the correction nearing its final stages, though Semiconductors could still fall another 10 to 15% before finding support around mid-November, and his year-end S&P 500 target stays 8,000. Separately, prediction markets put a 66% probability on a Democratic midterm sweep, and Morgan Stanley sees top global hoteliers outgrowing luxury goods makers, about 20% annual EPS growth through 2028 versus 10%.
